title: Vidur: A Large-Scale Simulation Framework For LLM Inference
technique: METRIC-PAPER: LLM inference performance simulator (operator-level profiling + predictive models, hierarchical scheduler) plus Vidur-Search, which picks the deployment configuration maximizing QPS per dollar under TTFT-P90 / TBT-P99 SLOs and a P99 scheduling-delay capacity definition

optimized_metrics.evidence: Vidur-Search helps the operator maximize QPS per dollar. Consider a deployment with 16 A100 GPUs. Capacity of the system is defined as the maximum queries per second that it can support without the queuing delay blowing up. Specifically we constrain the P99 scheduling delay to be under 5 seconds. This QPS value is divided by the cost of renting 16 A100 GPUs per hour to get the QPS per dollar value.

headline_claim.text: it estimates inference latency with less than 9% error across the range. Further, we present Vidur-Search, a configuration search tool that helps optimize LLM deployment. Vidur-Search uses Vidur to automatically identify the most cost-effective deployment configuration that meets application performance constraints.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we compare the percentage error of Vidur predictions for normalized end-to-end latency, which captures the request's end-to-end latency divided by its output length (Yu et al., 2022; Kwon et al., 2023).
metric_definitions.notes: divides by output length only; for static workloads the paper uses request execution time excluding scheduling delay

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Request-level metrics. These include per-request metrics such as the scheduling delay, prefill completion time, time-to-first-token (TTFT), and time-between-tokens (TBT).
metric_definitions.notes: TTFT and TBT never formally defined; listed as simulator outputs

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Capacity of the system is defined as the maximum queries per second that it can support without the queuing delay blowing up. Specifically we constrain the P99 scheduling delay to be under 5 seconds.
metric_definitions.notes: capacity defined via P99 scheduling delay <5s (found by binary search on QPS), not via TTFT/TBT SLOs

metric_definitions.definition_quote: This QPS value is divided by the cost of renting 16 A100 GPUs per hour to get the QPS per dollar value.
metric_definitions.notes: capacity QPS / GPU rental $ per hour

metric_definitions.definition_quote: cluster (Model FLOPs utilization, KV-Cache utilization, etc.) performance metrics
metric_definitions.notes: MFU and KV-cache utilization; not formalized

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We use a more relaxed constraint of P90 for TTFT since it is a one time delay experienced by the user, as opposed to TBT which is recurrent for each output token.
metric_definitions.notes: rationale for using P90 on TTFT vs P99 on TBT

metric_critiques.critique_quote: configurations which are optimal on one metric may not satisfy the SLO constraint on the other metric (these are the blue points on the Pareto curve).

small changes in latency SLOs can result in a significant cost overhead. For example, for the LLaMA2-70B-LMSys-Chat1M workload, if the TBT SLO is changed from 0.12 seconds to 0.14 seconds (a difference of only 20ms), the Pareto curve point moves from approximately 0.07 to 0.13, ~1.85x reduction in cost!

recommended_practice.quote: We use a more relaxed constraint of P90 for TTFT since it is a one time delay experienced by the user, as opposed to TBT which is recurrent for each output token.

Vidur achieves high fidelity (< 5% error) in almost all scenarios with request rate set to 85% of the system capacity – which is reflective of real production scenarios. Note that, as we approach capacity point, any small error in execution time prediction gets amplified

any system configuration will have a maximum QPS capacity for a given workload at which it can process the input requests without accumulating the request queue. We use this property to find the maximum QPS supported by a system via a simple binary search

slo_spec: TTFT P90 < 2 s and TBT P99 < 200 ms (what-if analysis); capacity = max QPS with P99 scheduling delay < 5 s
load_regime: Poisson arrivals at 85% (and 95%) of capacity for fidelity; QPS binary search for capacity; static offline traces
tradeoff_acknowledged: Throughput vs latency vs cost: SLO tightening raises cost (TBT SLO 0.12->0.14 s gives ~1.85x cost reduction); configs Pareto-optimal on TTFT may violate TBT SLO
hardware: A100 and H100 (profiled); up to 16 GPUs in search
extractor_notes: Simulator paper; its own fidelity metric is percentage error of (median and P95) normalized E2E latency. Vidur-Search objective is QPS/$ with SLO constraints; TTFT and TBT used but never formally defined.
